ui.intro: Configure NPCs once, then create them locally or use the same intent for an AI-generated Foundry payload.
ui.roleHint: Search or browse the hierarchical role catalog. The picker is virtualized so it stays responsive as the catalog grows.
ui.tierHint: Named competence tier. Change Tier style in Configure Settings to use exact CR values instead.
ui.challengeRatingHint: Choose any standard D&D 5e CR from 0, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, and 1 through 30.
ui.raceHint: Search or browse preset races. To use any other race, type its name into the picker search and select the custom entry.
ui.useCustomRace: Use this text as a custom Race
ui.namingStyleHint: Search or browse naming palettes. The Help window shows clearly distinct examples for each style.
ui.wealthHint: Influences AI-generated money, equipment quality, personal possessions, and status items.
ui.seedPlaceholder: Optional reproducible seed for local generation
ui.seedHint: Local generation with the same options and seed reproduces the same generated data.
ui.destinationIntro: Choose where locally generated or AI-imported Actors are created.
ui.destinationHint: Browse the full Actor-folder hierarchy, choose the Actors root or configured default, or type a new root-folder name into search and select it.
ui.createRootFolder: Create or reuse a new root Actor folder with this name
ui.openLastActorHint: Opens up to 10 Actors. Up to three are visible side-by-side; later Actors are stacked behind them so closing a top sheet reveals the next one.
ui.aiIntro: Copy a detailed strict prompt into any AI conversation, copy its JSON reply, then import that reply into the destination above.
ui.singleAiObject: Use a single JSON object when Count is 1
ui.singleAiObjectHint: Off by default. Otherwise the prompt always requests a JSON array, including for a single NPC.
ui.manualPastePlaceholder: Paste the JSON reply here only if your browser blocks clipboard reading.
ui.groupTypeHint: Create independent NPCs or a coherent family, patrol, raider band, crew, caravan, council, and other group archetypes.
ui.habitatHint: Choose the environment and settlement context that shapes daily life, possessions, travel, and social assumptions. Type any other habitat to use it directly.
ui.useCustomHabitat: Use this text as a custom habitat
ui.groupConfigurationIntro: Advanced controls for relationships, internal structure, race mixing, and shared group context.
ui.suggestedGroupSizesHint: Shortcuts only; Count remains fully editable.
ui.raceCompositionHint: Use the main Race field for a single-race group or as the primary race when mixing several races.
ui.possibleRacesHint: Search and select any number of allowed races. Custom races can be added by typing them into the search.
ui.raceDistributionHint: Controls how strongly the primary Race dominates the generated group.
ui.raceWeightsHint: Relative weights; they do not need to add up to 100.
ui.groupBriefPlaceholder: Optional: local feud, family business, employer, current crisis, taboo, destination, shared objective…
ui.groupBriefHint: Passed into the AI prompt as additional context. Keep it focused on facts that should affect multiple NPCs.

help.title: NPC Button Help
help.generationBody: The dashboard uses the same intent for deterministic local generation and the AI prompt workflow.
help.count: Type any allowed number directly, or use the common 1, 3, 5, and 10 shortcuts.
help.role: Defines the NPC's practical function and biases local ability scores and durability. It also strongly guides AI inventory and characterization.
help.tierStyleNamed: The world currently uses named tiers. Ordinary through Champion provide broad competence bands; Configure Settings can switch the world to exact CR selection.
help.tierStyleCr: The world currently uses CR tiers. Every standard D&D 5e CR from 0 through 30 is selectable and the AI prompt requests that exact CR.
help.race: The built-in Race picker contains all standard 2024 Player’s Handbook races. Typing a non-preset name offers it directly as a custom Race; mixed groups can select several preset or custom races.
help.wealth: Poor, Average, Well-Off, or Elite. The AI uses this to scale carried money, equipment quality, comfort items, and visible status.
help.seed: Only affects deterministic local generation. It is intentionally not required for AI generation.
help.destination: The folder picker preserves the Actor hierarchy. It can target any nested folder, the Actors root, the configured default, or a newly named root folder.
help.pickersBody: Role, Race, Naming style, Habitat, Group type, Tier/CR, Actor folder, and mixed-race selection use searchable hierarchical lists. Large lists render only visible rows plus a small buffer so catalog growth and large folder trees remain responsive.
help.namingBody: Naming styles are broad fictional tonal palettes rather than historical or linguistic claims. Each style now includes a larger set of creative idiomatic examples; the same examples and style guidance are embedded into the copied AI prompt as tonal references rather than a finite name list.
help.actorReviewBody: When review opening is enabled, the module opens at most the first 10 created Actors. Up to three top sheets are arranged side-by-side. Additional sheets reuse those column positions behind the first row, so closing a top sheet exposes the next Actor in that stack.
help.aiBody: The module does not call an AI service itself. It creates a strict portable prompt carrying naming references, habitat, group structure, race mixture, wealth, relationship density, secrets, rumours, quirks, and inventory requirements; then it validates the returned Actor core and inventory requests before import.
help.aiStep1: Configure Count, Group type, Habitat, Role, Tier or CR, Race composition, Wealth, Naming style, and Destination.
help.aiStep2: Click Copy prompt and paste the prompt into an AI conversation.
help.aiStep3: Copy the AI's JSON-only reply to your clipboard.
help.aiStep4: Return to Foundry and click Import NPC. The current destination is applied locally.
help.aiValidation: The importer rejects malformed or count-mismatched payloads before creating Actors. Canonical item lookups are resolved against D&D 5e equipment packs, while invented roleplay possessions remain safe loot Items.
help.groupType: Choose independent NPCs or an intentional group archetype. Group presets vary responsibilities and tell the AI to create shared history and useful internal roles instead of copies of one NPC.
help.habitat: Defaults to Forest Village. Habitat changes the expected daily life, possessions, travel assumptions, work, rumors, and social context.
help.standardRacesBody: The built-in Player’s Handbook 2024 catalog is: {races}. Custom races remain available through the same picker.
help.habitatsBody: Built-in environments cover ordinary settlements and more specialized regions, including {habitats}. Any other habitat can be typed as a custom entry.
help.groupsBody: Group presets include {groups}, plus further security, outlaw, travel, work, faith, and community structures. Count stays editable, while each preset exposes sensible size shortcuts.
help.groupsAdvanced: Advanced settings control family structure, cohesion, hierarchy, relationship density, internal conflict, allowed races, race distribution, custom weights, and an optional shared group brief.
help.portraitPromptBody: Generated or AI-imported NPC Actor sheets include a header button that copies a concise portrait prompt for exactly one full-body adult-anime image of that NPC.
help.filterBody: Configure Settings now provides a dedicated filter menu with allow/deny exact, contains, prefix, suffix, and regex rules for major picker-based dashboard fields.

notifications.gmOnly: Only a Game Master can create NPCs with Runyth NPC Button.
notifications.promptCopied: AI NPC prompt copied to the clipboard.
notifications.portraitPromptCopied: Portrait prompt copied to the clipboard.

errors.clipboardWrite: Clipboard writing is not available in this client.
errors.clipboardRead: Clipboard reading is not available or was blocked by the browser.
errors.manualPasteFallback: Open the manual-paste section, paste the AI JSON there, and click Import NPC again.

namingDescriptions.central: Balanced town-and-road names with restrained surnames; broadly settled and neutral in tone.
namingDescriptions.coastal: Open-vowel given names and maritime surnames suggesting ports, fishing communities, and sea trade.
namingDescriptions.highland: Harder consonants and landscape-heavy surnames suggesting uplands, stone settlements, and old local lineages.
namingDescriptions.frontier: Short practical names and occupational or settlement surnames suggesting farms, trades, border villages, and new communities.

filters.title: NPC Button string filters
filters.intro: Use allow and deny rules to curate the visible picker catalogs. Enter multiple values separated by commas, semicolons, or new lines. If any allow rule is configured for a category, entries must match at least one allow rule and must not match any deny rule.

placeholders.roles: Filter visible role entries by id, label, description, or search text.
placeholders.races: Filter visible race entries, including extension races and custom picker suggestions.
placeholders.namingStyles: Curate which naming palettes may be selected in the dashboard.
placeholders.habitats: Restrict or focus the environment presets shown in the habitat picker.
placeholders.groupTypes: Allow or hide specific group archetypes such as families or guard patrols.
placeholders.folders: Curate which Actor-folder targets appear in the destination picker.
